A note about delivery windows

Pallet Lane has been moving freight around the Upper Midwest since 2009, when our founder bought two used box trucks and a phone line. Back then every customer was on a first-name basis with their driver. We've grown a lot since then, from two trucks to thirty-one, and we're proud of that.

Lately we have been asking what customers value most. Reliability comes up in every survey we run, ahead of price. Customers want to know that when we say we're coming, we're coming.

You'll still get a text 30 minutes before arrival.

If a four-hour window doesn't work for your dock, call us. We can set up a fixed appointment for loads that need one, at no extra charge for existing accounts.

Thank you for your continued trust in us as we continue to grow.

prompt:
This is the section of our volunteer handbook that new people get. Nobody reads it, it's way too long. Can you cut it down to about 500 words? Don't lose anything that actually matters.

Welcome to Tidewater Food Pantry

Welcome, and thank you so much for giving your time to Tidewater Food Pantry! We are truly grateful that you have decided to join our wonderful team of volunteers. Our pantry has been serving neighbors in the Tidewater area for over twenty years, and none of it would be possible without people like you. This section of the handbook is meant to help you feel prepared and confident on your very first shift, and to answer the questions that new volunteers most often ask us. Please take a few minutes to read it carefully, and keep it handy so that you can refer back to it whenever you need to.

Our mission and values

At Tidewater Food Pantry, we believe that everyone deserves access to good food, and that everyone deserves to be treated with dignity while getting it. We are a pantry that believes in community, respect, and kindness. Every person who walks through our door is a neighbor, not a case. We ask all volunteers to keep these values in mind during every interaction, whether you are stocking shelves, packing bags, or greeting clients at the door. Our values guide everything we do, from how we arrange the shelves to how we say good morning.

Shifts and arriving

We have three regular shifts each week: Tuesday and Thursday from 9:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m., and Saturday from 8 to 11 in the morning. Please plan to arrive 15 minutes before your shift starts so that you have time to sign in, put your belongings away, and hear the shift lead's briefing. Being on time is really important to us because clients are often already waiting outside, and the pantry opens its doors to clients exactly at the start of each shift. When you arrive, please come in through the side door, not the front door, which is reserved for clients. You will find a tablet just inside the side door where you should sign in with your name every time you come. The sign-in is important because it helps us keep track of volunteer hours and lets us know who is in the building in case of an emergency.

If you cannot make a shift that you have signed up for, please let us know at least 24 hours in advance by emailing volunteers@tidewaterpantry.example or calling 555-0142. We understand that life happens and sometimes things come up, and we will never hold it against you. However, we really do depend on having enough people each week, so as much notice as you can give us is hugely appreciated. If you are ill, please stay home. You should not volunteer if you have had a fever, vomiting or diarrhea in the previous 48 hours.

What to wear

Please wear comfortable clothes that you don't mind getting a bit dusty, as we do a lot of lifting and moving boxes. Closed-toe shoes are required for everyone, with no exceptions, because of the risk of dropped cans and crates. Long hair should be tied back. Aprons and gloves are provided by the pantry, and you should wear disposable gloves whenever you handle fresh produce or open packages. Please wash your hands with soap and warm water for at least 20 seconds when you arrive, after any break, after using the restroom, and any time you change tasks. Handwashing is one of the most important things we can do to keep our clients safe.

Food safety

Food safety is the most important responsibility we have as volunteers, so please read this section especially carefully and ask your shift lead if anything is unclear.

The walk-in cooler must be kept at 41°F or below at all times. At the start of every shift, the shift lead checks the thermometer and writes the temperature on the log sheet hanging on the cooler door. If the temperature is ever above 41°F, do not take any food out of the cooler or put any in. Tell the shift lead right away. Please do not try to fix the cooler yourself.

There are certain items we cannot accept or hand out. Please do not put any food on the shelves that is open, home-canned or homemade, or past its "use by" date. For shelf-stable items with a "best by" date, we are able to distribute them up to six months past that date, as long as they are in perfect condition. Please discard any can that is bulging, leaking, or has a dented seam, as these can be signs of contamination. A can with a small dent in the body but not on the seam is fine to use. When in doubt, ask your shift lead, because it is always better to ask than to guess. If you are not sure about an item, set it on the gray cart marked "Ask" so the shift lead can review it later.

We also keep a separate, clearly labeled shelf for items that are peanut-free and gluten-free, so that clients with allergies can find them easily. Please always return these items to that shelf, and never mix them in with the rest of the stock.

Working with clients

Our clients come to us for many different reasons, and it is not our place to ask. Please never ask a client why they need food. Never take photographs of clients or of the line outside, even if you think it is harmless. If a client seems upset, stay calm and kind, and get the shift lead. Please do not share any information about our clients with anyone, including with other volunteers outside of the pantry. Mostly, just say hello, smile, and offer to carry bags to the car if they would like the help.

Safety and emergencies

The two emergency exits are the side door and the loading dock door at the back of the building. The fire extinguisher is on the wall by the kitchen, and the first aid kit is on the shelf above the sign-in tablet. In an emergency, call 911 first and then tell the shift lead. Please report any injury, no matter how small, to the shift lead so that it can be written in the incident log.

A quick checklist

Before you go, here is a short reminder of the most important points. Arrive 10 minutes before your shift. Sign in on the tablet at the side door. Wear closed-toe shoes. Wash your hands. Keep the cooler at 41°F or below. Ask when in doubt. And please let us know at least 24 hours ahead if you cannot make it.

Thank you again for being part of the Tidewater family. We are so excited to have you with us, and we can't wait to meet you!
rubric: The cut version is roughly 450 to 550 words (clearly shorter than the original), and is complete: every section has real content and nothing is left half-cut.

Keeps the specifics a volunteer needs to act safely and correctly: shift days and times, the side-door sign-in on the tablet, closed-toe shoes, the cooler limit of 41°F and telling the shift lead if it is higher, discarding bulging, leaking or seam-dented cans, no open or home-canned food, the 24-hour cancellation rule with the email and phone number, no photos of clients, and the emergency exits and 911 step.

Removes the right material: the welcome and closing pleasantries, the values paragraph that restates itself, and repeated explanations, rather than cutting facts or just trimming a little from every sentence.

Notices that the original gives two different arrival times (15 minutes before in one place, 10 minutes in the checklist) and flags it or resolves it openly for the user to confirm, instead of silently picking one.
Keeps the handbook's friendly, direct tone and uses plain headings or short sections so it can be skimmed; does not turn into a cold bullet dump.
Adds no new rules, numbers or contacts; anything the model dropped that the user might want back is mentioned in a line or two, not hidden.
